Parts concatenate exactly with no implicit separators. Include the whitespace required for headings, paragraphs, tables and other Markdown at every part boundary; a new heading needs a preceding newline. Keep local caveats associated with the same option. Slot values already contain some units: show points/currency/unit labels once and preserve minor-unit qualifiers; never infer missing fees, quote scope or totals. Describe source carriers as reported carriers unless operating-carrier evidence is explicit. Use exact supplied claim-catalog proposition names where applicable, rather than inventing synonymous machine labels; do not force an inapplicable proposition. Briefly explain why each selected variant is useful and distinct without adding eligibility or valuation policy. Explain coverage limitations in plain language while retaining mandatory source-bound disclosures. You still own layout, ordering and prose.

Binding reminders from the existing Results check contract (content obligations, not a layout): Each selected complete journey must visibly use these exact slots somewhere in parts with that journey reference_id: status, styles, route, departure, arrival, elapsed, award_program, award_route, award_departure, award_arrival, award_carrier, award_cabin, award_leg_cabins, points, fees, award_price_scope, price_completeness, booking_obligation, requirements, award_observed_at. Include award_mixed_cabin_pct or cash_mixed_cabin_pct if that component reports a value. Supply a visible stable identifier or use journey_id. For the selected direct cash benchmark use observation_id, disposition, route, departure, arrival, observed_at, provider_updated_at, cash, price_scope, carrier, cabin, leg_cabins. In shared parts use provider_status, coverage, complete_journey_count, benchmark_status. Copy each binding literally as {{fact:key}}. Natural-language paraphrases and disclosures metadata do not satisfy these slot checks. Use only available keys for the exact scope; benchmark has no duration slot. Each claim.text must be a verbatim visible sentence in its part, not a paraphrase, machine label or interpolation. For ordinary journey claims scope_ids must contain only that part reference_id; comparisons need their full supplied comparison pool. Do not invent predicates to make unsupported statements appear checked. In correction, address every reported failure with the exact binding, identity, or literal text it requests before making unrelated selection changes. You still choose layout, distinct valid admitted/conditional options, prose and grouping; rejected alternatives remain excluded with status and requirements bound if discussed.

Keep each factual slot's visible label faithful to its meaning: cash_cabin is cabin evidence, cash_leg_cabins is leg-cabin evidence, and neither is a carrier. Do not substitute those slots for unavailable carrier bindings. Describe source carriers as reported carriers only when a carrier slot supplies them. Declare material assertions you actually author about cabin, protection, quote scope, eligibility, or comparisons; copy each claim.text exactly from a visible sentence in that same part. Do not omit claim declarations merely to avoid checks, and do not add assertions to satisfy a claim quota. Use a catalog proposition only when the sentence affirms its exact meaning: 'protection is unverified' is not protected_connection; 'requirements remain' is not no_unresolved_requirements; 'party total is unknown' is not party_total. When an actual sentence has no applicable catalog predicate, use a truthful descriptive noncatalog proposition; it remains unchecked, never supported by default. Narrow option-to-option comparisons that are not whole-pool fastest/cheapest can be declared as kind other with that journey's exact scope_id, without pretending to be a full-pool ranking claim. A part's claims may be empty only when it contains factual bindings and connective wording without a material authored assertion. Ground every relative explanation in the exact attribute being compared: an earlier destination arrival does not imply an earlier origin departure, and identical departures must never be described as different.
